title: Eight plant origin contrasts did not reject mixed-rate decay at shared warm sites
abstract: We give a test of community adjustment that does not fit a response rate. If two origins at one destination share a constant symmetric positive semidefinite relaxation operator, their difference removes any shared target history. Its projection on the initial difference is a positive mixture of decaying exponentials. It must decrease and be convex, even with different species rates. We use cross-products of independent plot histories to remove initial-state sampling covariance. Eight TransPlant origin contrasts in five gradients gave four study clusters. Absolute-cover curvature was -0.054 of initial separation, with 97.5% cluster bootstrap limits -0.291 to 0.442. The increase score was -0.172 (-1.011 to 0.351). Neither rejected the model; substantial violations remain unresolved. Occurrence had a declining, convex source signal. This is a rate-free method and a limited null field test, not evidence that a lag explains the thermal tracking gap. Few clusters, selected complete histories, unknown block dependence and possible origin-specific targets limit inference. Code, proof, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Left: curvature scores and 95% cluster intervals. Thin outer line: 97.5% primary interval. Positive scores violate convex decay. Right: corrected absolute-cover pair trajectories, with actual relative census times. These are origin projections, not thermal tracking fractions.
